A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete MALA/MAViT paper, including Appendices A–B and references. Text and rendered content match throughout, except for the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original MALA/MAViT benchmark results, inference measurements, and ablations in Section 4, including ImageNet classification results in Table 2.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results in Section 4, including benchmark comparisons, inference measurements, and component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical MALA procedure, including the beta scaling factor, gamma offset, kernel transformation, and attention computation. No model component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same image classification, detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, NLP, speech recognition, and image generation tasks. ImageNet-1K, ADE20K, and the four NLP benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparison tables and figures retain identical comparator membership. This includes the same linear-attention baselines within each DeiT-T, Swin-T, and Swin-S setting in Table 9.

E3.justification: All reported protocols remain identical, including 300-epoch ImageNet training, the detection schedules, the 0.3B NLP model trained on 15B tokens, and 400K diffusion training iterations. Metrics and inference-timing conditions also match.

E4.justification: The query-normalization experiment in Table 1, attention and component ablations in Tables 9–11, and attention visualizations are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same natural-image examples and analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 1–11 and the appendix visualizations. For example, MAViT-L retains 86.0% ImageNet top-1 accuracy in Table 2, and MALA retains FID 49.62 in Table 8.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and the detailed derivations in Appendix A, Equations 15–22, are identical. The positive-attention assumptions and proof of the attention-ratio inequality are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about magnitude neglect, MALA's attention distribution, MAViT, and performance and efficiency across tasks.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations connecting query magnitude, attention concentration, and locality. Section 3.3 also preserves the qualification that negative or zero attention scores are theoretically possible but were not observed in the specified vision experiments.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, A100 timing conditions, and implementation disclosures are identical. Both retain the same prospective code-release statement and repository link.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements, and all 58 numbered references are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship is added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1, dated 1 July 2025, to v3, dated 2 August 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and organization, including its appendices, are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–11 retain identical graphics, formatting, captions, and placement. The document layout is unchanged; the margin-stamp text update is recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, experimental evidence, proofs, appendix analyses, and presentation are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility.
